races.name: Racing TV EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Happy Birthday Katie Exon Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Great
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two wins and three places from 14 runs on similar Good ground; Shane Gray fits a big yard outside connection here, but the 6f habit and redistribution into midfield rather than genuine rear position means it needs more pace than Beerwah is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out after a string of modest efforts, has run over today's trip and going before, and is fresh again 11 days on. Narrowly ahead at the head of our rating and the one to beat on the book form here.

runners_data.name: Dc Cogent
runners_data.note: Bryan Smart's 4-year-old is a hold-up type with a modest recent record — zero wins and two places from 15 sim-going runs — and a 34-day absence; Ben Robinson takes over but the raw form figures on 5f Good are uninspiring and it will need a strong pace to land a blow from the back.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in six runs this term but rarely far away, with two thirds among those finishes and a strong speed figure supporting the case. Has raced over today's trip before, though a 34-day layoff and a modest official mark count against it.

runners_data.name: Hurt You Never
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls and son Jack (5lb claim) team up with this veteran 7-year-old who has outstanding sim-going exposure — 15 from 15 runs on similar ground — and posted two wins and four places; genuine hold-up style that benefits from any pace scenario above a crawl, and the claim is meaningful.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in six starts and often held up towards the rear, though a third five starts back shows there is some ability there. Fit again 11 days on and has run over today's trip and going before, but needs to find more to trouble this field.

runners_data.name: Level Up
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald is a major booking for David Evans' 7-year-old, who shows solid recent placed form (three seconds and a third in the last five), and carries a tongue tie; a true hold-up horse placed into midfield by the field's congestion at the rear, so its best tactical chance evaporates if it cannot find its natural wide closing berth.
runners_data.comment: Frequently in the frame without getting his head in front, with three seconds and two thirds from his last six starts. Has run over today's trip and going before and returns 22 days after his last outing, needing to find the extra yard to open his account.

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 7-year-old has won three and placed six times from 15 sim-going runs and was successful just 11 days ago over this trip on Good; David Allan rides and the form is live, but it is a genuine hold-up type running in a race with limited pace, and its STYLE_FIT reflects that it may be forced to race more prominently than ideal — a double-edged factor given its recent win.
runners_data.comment: Won four starts back before two runner-up efforts underlined the improvement, though a below-par seventh last time out is a blot on the record. Back in action just 5 days later, and has run over today's trip and going before - capable of better than that.

runners_data.name: Beerwah
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner, with two wins from 15 sim-going runs; Jack Callan (3lb claim) has ridden it before and will aim to dominate from the front on this flat 5f, and the blinkers sharpen focus — but STYLE_FIT of 0.93 flags that even the leader can be compromised when forced into a role outside its comfort zone against a big field.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out for a second success in his last five starts, and has already run over today's trip and going. A 25-day gap since and a modest speed figure make him hard to trust against these on the ability shown so far.

runners_data.name: Toptime
runners_data.note: S R Bowring's veteran 8-year-old has won on Good ground at 5f and finished third last time out; George Wood takes the ride and the 39-day break is the main question mark, but as a genuine prominent type it is well-placed to track Beerwah and benefit if the leader tires.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, having also landed a race five starts back, with a third, a fourth and an unplaced effort sandwiched between the two victories. Has run over today's trip and going before, but a 39-day break since raises a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Bibendum
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 5-year-old won last time out (OR=61, 5f Good) and wears a visor; Ryan Sexton rides, and as a genuine prominent racer it is ideally drawn to sit second or third and sprint home — the good recent form and Going profile make it one of the more likely beneficiaries of Scenario A.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, but that success followed four losing efforts on the bounce, including two unplaced runs, in the runs before it. Has run over today's trip and going before, though that modest recent scoreline makes it hard to trust the upturn just yet.

runners_data.name: Dandy Dinmont
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's 7-year-old won over this C&D trip on Good last time out, which is an obvious tick, but its true running style is hold-up and this race lacks the pace to set it up; Rowan Scott is a capable claimer but the STYLE_FIT discount and the field's congestion at the rear both weigh against it finding the same position it did when winning.
runners_data.comment: Won four starts back and rates well above his current official mark on our figures, suggesting more to come. Fit again 13 days on and has run over today's trip and going before, though the finishing figures either side of that win have been modest.

runners_data.name: Opal Storm
runners_data.note: Brian Rothwell's 6-year-old is a hold-up horse with no wins or places from six runs on Good going, returning just six days after its last run; Faye McManoman rides and the headgear (tongue-tie, pads) suggests a tricky character — the combination of poor sim-going form, redistribution out of role, and lowest OR in the field makes this the hardest runner to make a case for.
runners_data.comment: Won four starts back but has since fallen away, beaten a long way in three of her last four including eighth last time out. Quick to reappear 6 days on, has run over today's trip and going before, but sits bottom of this field on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Beerwah is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only Toptime and Bibendum as genuine prominent types to push up alongside, is likely to secure a comfortable lead through the early stages on this flat Beverley 5f. The pace will be honest but controlled — Beerwah has won twice at the trip on Good ground and Jack Callan will aim to dictate from the off, creating a steady-to-fair gallop rather than a scorching tempo. This shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or travel just off the pace and sustain their effort, rather than deep closers needing a strong pace to aim at. The field holds more hold-up types than can all get their natural position: Level Up, Dream Deal, Dandy Dinmont, Opal Storm, and to a degree Great and Dc Cogent are all redistrubuted toward midfield, meaning genuine hold-up running in the final furlong is the least reliable scenario here — those horses will be racing further forward than suits them and cannot count on the strong pace a true closer needs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beerwah Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Beerwah leads without serious early pressure and the pace is fair but not suicidal, prominent racers tracking close to the leader hold every advantage.
scenarios.body: Beerwah sets a manageable tempo on Good to Firm ground, with Toptime and Bibendum tracking in second and third, and the race is run to suit those who race close to affairs throughout; the hold-up horses redistrubuted into midfield arrive too late or lack the pace to peel wide and close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace, Front Falls Late
scenarios.trigger: If Toptime or Bibendum press Beerwah hard enough to raise the tempo, setting up a stronger-than-expected gallop that finds out the leader in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Beerwah's effort burns out close home after dictating throughout, and a horse travelling just behind the leader — ideally one with a high sim-going strike rate on this surface — picks up the pieces; Dream Deal or Level Up, racing further forward than natural, could benefit if they take a prominent berth.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to stretch the field and create a gap for well-handicapped midfield horses to exploit in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Horses like Hurt You Never or Great, both with solid sim-going form on Good ground, get a strong enough gallop to close into, but the limited pace dynamic here makes this scenario reliant on conditions that this field is unlikely to generate spontaneously.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Deep Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race somehow develops into a genuine burn-up from the front and the leaders tie each other up, leaving a rare window for the redistributed hold-up horses to finish past beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: This depends on horses like Dandy Dinmont, Opal Storm, or Level Up producing their best closing style in a race where they are unlikely to get their natural position and where the pace setup does not favour them; the low STYLE_FIT scores for several of these runners reduce this scenario's credibility markedly.

watchPoints.text: Beerwah's early supremacy is the fulcrum of this race — watch whether Jack Callan gets a clean break and a clear lead; if Toptime or Bibendum crowd it for the early position, the whole pace dynamic shifts.

Dream Deal is declared five days after its last run and carries a tongue-tie and back tendon boots — any sign of a below-par warm-up or reluctance to stride out in the early stages should reduce its chance significantly despite its strong recent form.

Level Up and Dandy Dinmont both carry STYLE_FIT scores below 0.93 as redistributed hold-up types; watch their draw and whether PJ McDonald or Rowan Scott attempt to push them forward at the start rather than accept their natural off-the-pace position.

The Going Report consistently lists this race as Good to Firm across all six entries — faster than the declared Good, which may inconvenience horses whose sim-going form is based on softer conditions; Dc Cogent (Soft/Standard wins) and Toptime (two Soft wins) are most exposed if the ground is quick.

Hurt You Never has run on similar going in all 15 of its recent starts — a rare 15/15 sim-going hit rate — making it the standout ground specialist in the field; if the pace develops at all, the 5lb claim from Jack Nicholls becomes a live asset over the closing stages.

races.name: Skybet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: It Just Takes Time
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer at 7-8f on Good ground with five places from five runs in similar conditions; tracking the pace is its natural game and the uncontested gallop set by A War Eagle is ideal for a horse that travels smoothly and picks up in the straight — Jack Garritty knows the horse well.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in six starts but rarely out of the frame of late, with two seconds and a third among the latest finishes. Has run over today's trip and going before and returns just 16 days after his latest run, though the three finishes down the field are the concern.

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Has won off a higher mark at 8f on Good ground and Callum Rodriguez rides with confidence, but its hold-up style is structurally disadvantaged in a race with a single, steady pace-setter — it needs the front to soften, and there is nothing in this field to make that happen.
runners_data.comment: Won four starts back and has since been a mixed bag, returning to form when runner-up last time out. Has run over today's trip and going before, and a repeat of that best form would make him hard to hold out in this small field.

runners_data.name: A War Eagle
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, and a 45-day absence is the principal risk — it has shown a win and five places from 13 runs on Good or faster ground, but its stamina may be tested if the layoff has left it short; Billy Garritty must judge the fractions carefully to preserve enough for the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Won four starts back and has rarely been far away since, following a third last time out that kept the form ticking over. Has run over today's trip and going before, and although a 45-day absence is a small question, he rates the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form with two wins and two seconds from its last five, and Charlie Johnston's operation is firing (7/65 over 14 days); a natural front-runner who ideally wants to race prominently, though the presence of A War Eagle means it is unlikely to get that position cleanly — the style constraint is real even if the form is strong.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back and has been admirably consistent since, with three seconds and a third among his last six starts. Has run over today's trip and going before, and carries just 125 lb, giving him every chance in this small field.

runners_data.name: Coolree
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-strap and has five places from eight runs at 8f on Good or faster ground, but like Tattie Bogle it is a prominent racer squeezed out of its favoured berth by A War Eagle; Sam England's 2/11 strike rate over 14 days is modest, and racing further back than ideal makes this a tough assignment for a 69-rated horse.
runners_data.comment: A two-time winner from his last six starts, following up one success with another and boosted by a solid speed figure. Has run over today's trip and going before, but he sits bottom of this field on our figures, leaving plenty to prove against these rivals.

races.paceDynamic: A War Eagle is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners and no genuine challenger for the lead, will coast to the front unchallenged and set a sustainable, measured gallop over the 7½ furlongs on Good to Firm ground at Beverley. It Just Takes Time will track prominently just off the pace, while Glenfinnan is the race's lone genuine hold-up horse and will be anchored at the rear. Tattie Bogle and Coolree are both natural prominent racers who cannot all occupy that position simultaneously — A War Eagle is almost certain to secure the lead, and of the two redistributed types, Tattie Bogle's recent course-and-distance profile gives it the best claim to organise closest to the front, with Coolree likely to sit slightly further back than ideal. A single, uncontested pace-setter on fast ground over a staying-sprint trip creates a strongly pace-controlled shape that rewards horses who can travel smoothly just off the leader and pick up efficiently — the prominent-to-lead profile benefits most, and hold-up types like Glenfinnan face the significant burden of making up ground without any pace collapse to exploit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Wire to Wire
scenarios.trigger: If A War Eagle dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and the field never applies pressure through the early or middle stages.
scenarios.body: A War Eagle sets every fraction, conserves energy through the bend, and has enough in reserve to repel late challengers on the Good to Firm surface; the sustainable tempo means the leader is never put under the kind of early duress that would cause it to capitulate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Outstays Leader
scenarios.trigger: If A War Eagle's 45-day absence leaves it short of peak fitness and it ties up in the final furlong, allowing a prominent tracker to collar it.
scenarios.body: It Just Takes Time, tracking the pace throughout, is positioned to pounce when the leader weakens, having shown consistent placed form at this trip on similar going; Tattie Bogle, if able to secure a forward pitch despite the redistribution, also has the profile to benefit from this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is materially stronger than expected and the field tightens on the turn, creating enough of a compression in the final two furlongs for Glenfinnan to close.
scenarios.body: Glenfinnan is the only genuine hold-up horse in the field and has winning form on comparable going at 8f, so a genuine collapse of a contested pace is the one scenario that brings it into play; however, with a lone front-runner and no pressure horses, this scenario depends on conditions that this race shape is unlikely to produce.

watchPoints.text: A War Eagle's 45-day absence is the single biggest threat to Scenario A — watch how Billy Garritty manages the pace through the middle half-mile, as any sign of the horse feeling the race will open the door for It Just Takes Time.

Tattie Bogle and Coolree may both attempt to push forward at the start despite the redistribution — if either contests the early lead with A War Eagle, the pace dynamic changes materially and Glenfinnan's hold-up chance improves.

Glenfinnan's chance is almost entirely conditional on a pace collapse that this race shape is not set up to produce — monitor its starting price movement as a signal of any market intelligence about jockey tactics or going changes.

Good to Firm is confirmed for this race by the going report — all five runners have acceptable form on this surface, so no horse carries a meaningful going concern, and the fast ground will tend to sustain a clean, uncomplicated gallop that reinforces the front-runner's advantage.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Hull Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ice Show
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old has operated at 8-10f in recent runs and this 7½f trip looks on the short side; a hold-up runner with no wins or places on similar ground (0W0P in four sim-going runs), and 22 days off adds a question mark over sharpness.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out and without a win in four starts this campaign, rated the lowest of these at 49. Has run over today's trip and going before, but a run of finishes outside the frame leaves her needing to find significant improvement here.

runners_data.name: Bantz
runners_data.note: Alan Brown runner has placed on good ground and ran from prominent positions historically, but his true style is hold-up and with so many rivals seeking the same late ground he is squeezed for racing room tactically; 0/11 for trainer in 14 days is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out and without a win in his last five starts, form offering little encouragement. Ran only seven days ago and has run over today's trip and going before, but a rating of 50 leaves plenty to find here.

runners_data.name: Ryefield
runners_data.note: Lawrence Mullaney's three-year-old carries a flagged tendency to fade in the finish, which is a serious liability in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to bring the field back to him; 46-day absence and a step up from 5-6f trips makes the task steeper.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, with a fifth the best of those efforts. Has run over today's going before following a 46-day break, though a rating of 58 keeps him among the leading contenders here.

runners_data.name: King Sharja
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's six-year-old has back-to-back second-place finishes over 7f on good ground and is the one runner realistically able to sit close to Back From Dubai in the early stages; at OR 55 and with James Sullivan aboard, he is the most likely horse to exploit the stalking position if the leader fades.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts but was runner-up three and four starts back, and has run over today's trip and going before. Unplaced last time out, though a rating of 58 keeps him right in contention on his placed form.

runners_data.name: African Spirit
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' five-year-old wears a tongue-strap and is naturally a late-running type, but the crowded rear quarter of this field means he will need to make his effort wide and early; his best recent run was a third over 8f on good ground, suggesting the 7½f on a faster surface may just find him out.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out — the best of four starts without a win this campaign — and holds a rating of 61, the highest in the field. Has run over today's trip and going before, giving him solid claims to be involved in the finish.

runners_data.name: Back From Dubai
runners_data.note: S R Bowring's nine-year-old is the lone front-runner and holds the unique tactical advantage of being able to control tempo entirely unchallenged; he won over 7f on soft going 36 days ago and steps into a race where his role as sole pace-setter gives him a structural edge well beyond his OR of 51.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out, but a winner three starts back, and third four starts back before that — proof he can be competitive. Has run over today's trip and going before, though a rating of 56 and a 36-day break leave plenty to find here.

runners_data.name: Walk On Walk On
runners_data.note: Noel Wilson's three-year-old has a 2/8f placing on good going and wears a hood, suggesting he can be keen; he is a natural hold-up runner competing in a race that gives him few favours, and Ryan Sexton will need to find a clear passage that may not materialise in a bunched rear group.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, his best effort in a run of six starts without a win, and rated 57 puts him firmly in this. Has run over today's trip and going before, giving him solid claims among the leading dangers here.

runners_data.name: Itszaboy
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's three-year-old has run six consecutive races without placing and all recent runs have come over 7-8f on good ground at similar level — the form line offers no confidence; naturally held up, he is effectively racing against his own style in this pace shape and Faye McManoman faces a positional challenge from the outset.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last five starts and yet to find the frame in that sequence, sixth his latest two efforts. Has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 52 leaves him with a lot to find against this field.

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: David Evans' three-year-old has the most consistently strong form figures in the field — five runs of 2-3-3-3-4 at around 8f on good ground — and P J McDonald is a major booking; she is a hold-up runner by nature and while the pace shape does not ideally suit her, her raw form gives her the best chance of any of the back-markers if even a modest late run is possible.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, continuing a consistent run of places, though it's been six starts since a win. Has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 53 puts her right in the mix without standing out.

races.paceDynamic: Back From Dubai is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push him from the outside, he is expected to dictate from the front at a sustainable, unhurried gallop over Beverley's 7½f trip on Good to Firm ground. That controlled tempo means the early fractions will be modest, favouring a horse who can travel close to the pace and kick off the home turn rather than one who needs a truly searching gallop to bring them into the race late. The majority of the field — Ice Show, Bantz, King Sharja, African Spirit, Walk On Walk On, Itszaboy and Alice's Influence — are all hold-up types by nature, which creates a structurally compressed race where the midfield and rear will be congested and few will get a true test of stamina. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or at least in the first third, tracking Back From Dubai without expending energy, and quicken from a position of comfort; deep hold-up horses face a tough ask to generate enough momentum off a slow fractions race to reel in a relaxed leader. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Walk On Walk On, African Spirit, Itszaboy, Bantz and Alice's Influence are all natural off-the-pace runners, but only Back From Dubai and perhaps King Sharja are realistically positioned to secure a forward berth from the outset.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Back From Dubai Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai bowls along unchallenged in front and sets an honest but not gruelling tempo that suits a front-to-finish winner.
scenarios.body: Back From Dubai has won over 7f on soft going and placed on good, and with no pressure he can control the race from wire to wire at his own pace; the compressed, hold-up-heavy field behind him will struggle to mount a sustained challenge off a soft gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalker Swoops Late Turn
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking closely in second or third uses the home turn to kick and catches Back From Dubai flattening out in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse positioned just off the leader's shoulder — ideally within two lengths turning in — would inherit the initiative when the leader's reserves are spent after controlling the race alone; the Good to Firm surface rewards those with a quick stride rather than pure stamina.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Bursts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves faster than anticipated and the field strings out, creating genuine late ground for a hold-up runner to pick up.
scenarios.body: A true off-the-pace type would need the leaders to have gone hard enough to tie themselves up, which is unlikely given Back From Dubai's unchallenged status; Alice's Influence has the most consistent form figures at around 8f on good ground and is the most credible candidate if pace does materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai is outpaced or withdrawn and a messy, slow-burn race produces a sprint finish with no clear beneficiary.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up types bunched together and no authoritative pace, the race could devolve into a scrappy final-furlong dash where positional luck and draw dominate over form; in this scenario horses with any ability to quicken from a handy position hold an edge over those needing a true test.

watchPoints.text: Watch Alice's Influence's draw and early position — P J McDonald is a top booking for a horse with five consecutive top-four finishes on good going, and if she can race closer than her natural style suggests she becomes the most dangerous threat to Back From Dubai.

Watch Back From Dubai's early stride pattern — if he jumps slowly or is taken on for the lead by any of the prominently-positioned types, his entire tactical advantage evaporates and the race becomes genuinely open.

Watch King Sharja at the start — he needs to break cleanly to take up his stalking position on Back From Dubai's heels, and with multiple rivals attempting to do the same, a sluggish break could leave him buried in a congested midfield with no clear run.

Watch the pace in the first three furlongs — on Good to Firm ground at Beverley, if Back From Dubai sets only a crawl, the sprint finish in the final two furlongs will be decided by luck in running and position rather than form, which scrambles the form book for all hold-up runners.

Watch Ryefield for any sign of prominent early racing — if Mullaney's runner attempts to race up with the pace rather than hold up as usual, the flagged tendency to fade in the finish becomes even more relevant in the straight.

races.name: Sky Bet For The Fans Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Elettaria
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up mare who has finished 4th, 3rd, and 7th in recent runs over 7-8f on good ground; trainer John Wainwright has a modest 1/3 14-day strike rate and 21 days since last run is not a concern, though she is working from a true hold-up position and the redistribution to midfield mapping means she will need things to fall right in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out having been third two starts back, a reasonably solid recent sequence without a win in six starts this campaign. Has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 51 keeps her in the frame among these dangers.

runners_data.name: Inspiring Speeches
runners_data.note: The lone pace-setter here, she carries headgear and drops in from 10-14f trips; Sara Ender's yard is in fair form (2/4 in 14 days), but her STYLE_FIT flag is a caution — she has been racing at a longer trip recently and her ability to sustain a true front-running role over this 1m½f trip on good-to-firm must be respected rather than assumed.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out and third two starts back, form that puts him among the more consistent without a win in five starts. Has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 54 gives him solid claims among the dangers here.

runners_data.name: Copper And Five
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old with a busy schedule (just 4 days since last run) who has been running consistently, placing twice in eight-furlong good-ground contests; Ruth Carr's yard is active (3/23) and Joanna Mason's claim could be useful — distance step to 1m½f is the query but the horse's recent second-place efforts show it is in form.
runners_data.comment: Eighth last time out but was runner-up four and five starts back, more encouraging placed form before that. Ran only four days ago and has run over today's trip and going before, with a rating of 55 keeping him among the dangers here.

runners_data.name: Defence Missile
runners_data.note: Four-year-old whose natural style is hold-up, pushed into a midfield map slot due to the volume of closers in this field; Linda Perratt has had no winners in 14 days (0/17), and the horse's recent form of 5-9-8-6-8 across 6-8f on good-to-soft is unencouraging — the step to 1m½f is untested territory.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out in a run of modest form, but holds a narrow rating edge over these rivals at 58. Has run over today's trip and going before, giving him the clearest claims of a moderate field despite unexceptional recent finishes.

runners_data.name: Mavetheforcebewivu
runners_data.note: Holds a visor in headgear (hg:v) and showed a single second-place effort at 8f on good ground among recent runs; Alan Brown is winless in 14 days (0/11), the horse is a true hold-up type mapped to midfield by necessity, and a form string of 7-0-7-2-0-9 at various distances makes confidence here difficult to sustain.
runners_data.comment: Ninth last time out and yet to win in six starts, though there was a runner-up effort three starts back. Ran only six days ago and has run over today's trip and going before, but the bottom rating of 41 leaves plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Ring Of Gold
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran wearing a visor, whose good-ground record is sparse (3 from 15 qualifying runs, 0 wins, 0 places); Michael & David Easterby's yard is active (4/31) but this horse's recent 7th, 7th and 13th-place finishes paint a bleak picture — it is a genuine hold-up type reassigned to midfield in the map and unlikely to land a telling blow.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out, a modest recent run though he was runner-up six starts back and has been competitive at times without a win. Has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 51 leaves him a fair, if unspectacular, midfield chance.

runners_data.name: Royal Sizzler
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old for Michael Dods (4/31 in 14 days) with Cieren Fallon taking the ride, which is an obvious stable positive; only 1 qualifying run from 4 on similar going (0 wins, 0 places), and the form string of 5-0-0-4 is thin — the horse carries the minimum 127lbs as the youngest in the field and the trip at 1m½f is a question mark, but jockey quality lifts its claims.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out but otherwise well beaten, without a win in four starts and rated only 42, second-bottom of this field. Has run over today's trip and going before, but there is little in her recent form to inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Inspiring Speeches is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 1m½f Beverley classified stakes and, with no obvious challenger for the lead, she should dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo on good-to-firm ground. That uncontested lead is significant — she can bowl along at her own rhythm, setting just enough pace to keep hold-up horses honest without burning herself out, which strongly favours her and any horse capable of tracking her through the race. The field is dominated by hold-up types, but Elettaria, Defence Missile, Mavetheforcebewivu and Ring Of Gold are all redistributed from the rear of the field — they are genuine hold-up horses pushed into a midfield mapping position simply because there are too many of them to represent individually at the back, and none of them are likely to challenge Inspiring Speeches for the front. This race shape — lone front-runner, true hold-up horses drawn deep behind, no genuine pace pressure — favours hold-up runners who can produce a sustained late run on a flat track, and Copper And Five, with solid recent form at the trip, is best placed to exploit a well-judged pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Inspiring Speeches Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Inspiring Speeches is allowed to control from the front without any early pressure and sets a steady-to-moderate tempo.
scenarios.body: She ticks along unchallenged, conserving energy through the middle portions of the race and putting rivals in a waiting game that stretches their finishing kicks; horses who can track and quicken over this longer trip benefit most from a steady early pace that suddenly quickens in the home straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If Inspiring Speeches's pace proves genuinely moderate and a hold-up horse picks up powerfully in the straight on the good-to-firm ground.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdled gallop compresses the field until the straight, where a horse with a strong sustained finish can swoop past a tiring leader; Copper And Five's recent form over 8f and Royal Sizzler's age profile make them the prime beneficiaries of a late-run scenario on fast ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Inspiring Speeches goes too fast for her own ability in trying to build an unassailable lead and fades in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A front-runner who overestimates her stamina on good-to-firm ground at 1m½f can blow up late, leaving the race open to the closest tracker; any horse that has shadowed the leader at close range rather than chasing from well back gains the decisive positional advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Midfield Affair
scenarios.trigger: If several redistributed hold-up types interfere with each other's runs and cause traffic issues in the straight.
scenarios.body: With multiple genuine hold-up horses all competing for late running room on a track that narrows their options, interference or a bunched finish becomes plausible; horses with the widest berth or who circumnavigate trouble — potentially Royal Sizzler or Ring Of Gold on outside draws — would benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Inspiring Speeches must be monitored from the gates — if she is slow away or another runner challenges early, the clean uncontested lead that underpins the dominant scenario disappears entirely.

Copper And Five was run just 4 days ago; watch the early market move closely to gauge trainer confidence that the horse has recovered fully, as quick-turnover runners over 1m½f on good-to-firm can flatten out late.

Cieren Fallon's booking for Royal Sizzler is the most eye-catching jockey appointment in this field — if the market shortens the three-year-old meaningfully before the off, treat it as a serious tactical alert given Dods's 4/31 14-day form.

With four genuinely redistributed hold-up horses (Elettaria, Defence Missile, Mavetheforcebewivu, Ring Of Gold) all seeking late running room in the straight, watch for traffic issues and crowding as they fan out — horses drawn widest may have the cleanest passage.

Ring Of Gold's visor and 30-day absence, combined with a form record of 0 wins and 0 places from 15 runs on comparable going, warrants monitoring purely as a potential market drifter that could signal an intended absence of intent from connections.

races.name: Racing Again Next Tuesday Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sands
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over 10f on good ground for the Easterby yard make this confirmed leader compelling — she sets her own tempo from the front and rarely gets headed when allowed to bowl along; the step up to 1m2f at Beverley on fast ground looks ideal, and 21 days since last run is a typical winning gap for this horse.
runners_data.comment: Won his last two starts to round off a progressive campaign, with the form franked by a fourth and a third before that. Has run over today's trip and going before, and although 21 days have passed since that latest success, he rates clear of this field on the book.

runners_data.name: Mwafaq
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (three wins from last five) at 7f-8f on good ground gives him a solid profile, though stepping up to 1m2f is a genuine query given all his wins have come at shorter; Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim is a useful weight concession and he is likely to sit prominently just behind Shimmering Sands if the pace is sensible.
runners_data.comment: A prolific sort with three wins from his last five starts, including a success last time out, and already race-fit 17 days on. Has run over today's going before, but sits bottom of this field on our figures despite that record, leaving plenty to find against these rivals.

runners_data.name: Enamorus
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old has placed well on good ground but has not won at any of his last seven starts; Cieren Fallon takes over in the saddle and the hold-up style means he is entirely dependent on others setting a pace brisk enough to bring him into play from off it — the expected steady fractions are a material concern.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts but rarely disgraced, with two thirds - including last time out - and a second amongst the finishes. Has run over today's going before, and a sizeable gap to her official mark hints at more to come.

runners_data.name: Kitsune Power
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground last time out for Tim Easterby and the distance is clearly not an issue, but a hold-up style means he needs more pace than Shimmering Sands is likely to generate; the six-day turnaround is quick, though Easterby regularly runs this horse fresh and David Allan knows him well.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and races again quickly just 6 days later, with the form book showing a runner-up effort and a third among his recent starts too. Has run over today's trip and going before, and a wide gap to his current official mark suggests there is more improvement in hand.

runners_data.name: Ziata
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old is by nature a prominent racer but cannot get to the front here with Shimmering Sands in the field — that means she operates in unfamiliar territory for this race; her form in similar going is thin (1/5) and the style mismatch, combined with 33 days off, makes her a difficult proposition at the likely odds.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five starts but competitive throughout, with two thirds - including last time out - and a second amongst the finishes. Has run over today's trip before, and although 33 days have passed since her last outing, the gap to her official mark points to more improvement than that mark suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Shimmering Sands is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Mwafaq likely to press from a prominent position, she faces minimal early pressure over this 1m2f trip at Beverley on good-to-firm ground. With no genuine challenger to her lead, she is set to control fractions from the front and dictate a measured, sustainable gallop that will suit those with tactical speed rather than pure staying power. The field contains more prominent-profile runners than can physically occupy the front rank — Ziata, a natural prominent racer, has been redistributed to a midfield mapping because Shimmering Sands and Mwafaq will take up the positions ahead; Ziata is unlikely to secure her preferred pitch. This race shape strongly favours the front-running and genuinely prominent profiles: a controlled pace on fast ground at a track that rewards those who travel well throughout, with hold-up horses needing a meaningful injection of pace in the straight that may not materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shimmering Sands Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Shimmering Sands leads unchallenged at a measured gallop and kicks on rounding the home turn.
scenarios.body: Shimmering Sands dictates from flag to finish with Mwafaq the only rider close enough to apply pressure, and her recent back-to-back wins on good ground at 10f underline that this trip and surface suit her well. A controlled pace converts this into a test of tactical speed and class, benefiting those positioned prominently throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mwafaq Outkicks Up Front
scenarios.trigger: If Mwafaq tracks Shimmering Sands closely and finds the line-speed to overhaul her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Mwafaq's recent form of five wins from eight going forward and a sharp turn of foot on good ground make him a credible threat if he travels well on the heels of the leader. The pace will be soft enough that a prominent horse with acceleration wins comfortably, and Mwafaq's profile — multiple wins on good ground at shorter trips — means he may simply be quicker at the finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Best
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and Kitsune Power or Enamorus produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: With only two horses truly at the head of affairs, a very slow early pace could compress the field and allow Kitsune Power — who won over 10f on good ground last time — to loom dangerously late. Enamorus has the hold-up profile to benefit from a sprint finish, though both are relying on the front-runners setting a tempo fast enough to create exploitable ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Ziata Improves Into Midfield Role
scenarios.trigger: If Ziata adapts from her natural prominent style and produces a strong run from mid-division.
scenarios.body: Ziata is a genuine prominent type forced wider back in the field due to the race shape, and racing out of role reduces her chance materially; her sole placing in similar going (1/5 record) also tempers confidence. However, if the pace is honest enough to string the field out, her raw ability at this class level could still produce a notable late effort.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Mwafaq attempts to press Shimmering Sands early — if he does, it could inject enough pace to string the field and bring Kitsune Power into contention; if he sits off her, the leader becomes very hard to peg back.

Ziata's ability to adapt to a midfield role is uncertain — if she attempts to force her way to the front early, she risks burning out over this trip and disrupting the race shape for other prominent runners.

The going report consistently reads Good to Firm rather than the card's stated Good across all distances at Beverley tonight — horses with any going concern on fast ground should be treated with caution, particularly over this longer 1m2f trip.
Kitsune Power ran just six days ago — monitor market moves close to the off as a sharp support or drift will signal whether the Easterby team have targeted this race or are simply filling a slot.
